diagnostic_evidence.quote: We impose periodic boundary condition in \(x\) and zero-flux boundary condition in \(v\).
We distinguish the predicted density $\hat{\rho}^n$ from the true density $\rho^n$, defined through the moment of $f^n$, because the low-rank scheme introduced below does not strictly preserve mass.

issues.failure_explanation: On a periodic spatial domain the discrete Poisson equation $-\Delta_x\phi=\hat\rho^{n+1}-\eta$ is solvable only if the right-hand side has zero spatial mean. The prediction $\hat\rho^{n+1}=\rho^n+\Delta t\langle\mathcal A_h(f^n),1\rangle_v^h$ preserves the mean of $\rho^n$, but the paper itself states that the low-rank K–S–L evolution does not strictly preserve mass, so the mean of $\rho^n-\eta$ drifts away from zero after the first step (the K- and S-step Fokker–Planck contributions involve $P_V1\neq1$ and thus change the mass). The instruction 'Solve the Poisson equation using $\hat\rho^{n+1}$' then refers to a singular periodic Laplacian solve, and the same unmodified step appears in Algorithm 2.

failure_location.quote: Solve the Poisson equation using $\hat{\rho}^{n+1}$ for $E^{n+1}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: At each Poisson solve, replace $\hat\rho-\eta$ by its spatially mean-zero projection (or explicitly remove the drifting mean), and state this compatibility step in Algorithms 1 and 2.
issues.overall_effect: Algorithm 1 (and the identical prediction steps of Algorithm 2) is not guaranteed to be executable: once mass drift makes $\hat\rho^{n+1}-\eta$ non-neutral, $E^{n+1}$ and hence the whole time step are undefined as stated. Theorem 5.3 presupposes a well-defined $E^{n+1}$ but is not itself invalidated.
issues.title: Periodic Poisson solve in the low-rank schemes is not guaranteed solvable (mass drift breaks discrete neutrality)
issues.why_classification: A standard local compatibility fix (mean projection at the periodic Poisson solve) makes both algorithms well defined; the method, convergence orders, AP property, and all other guarantees are unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: Two written estimates fail. (a) From the Cauchy–Schwarz chain the proof only obtains $\bar u^2\le L_vM_{\max}\|u-\bar u\|^2$; since $\|\bar u\cdot 1\|_v^h=\sqrt{L_v}|\bar u|$, this supports $\|u\|^2\le(1+L_v\sqrt{M_{\max}})^2\|u-\bar u\|^2$, a factor $L_v$ weaker than the claimed $(1+\sqrt{L_vM_{\max}})^2$, so the displayed inference does not follow (the sharp bound $\|M\|_{v}^{h,2}\le M_{\max}$, from $\langle M,1\rangle_v^h=1$, is needed). (b) The pointwise Poincaré display $\mathcal D(u)\ge\lambda_N\|u-\bar u\|_{v}^{h,2}$ with $\mathcal D(u)=\Delta v^{-2}\sum(u_{q+1}-u_q)^2$ is false whenever $\Delta v>1$ (the sharp inequality is $\Delta v\,\mathcal D(u)\ge\lambda_N\|u-\bar u\|^2$), and the proof simultaneously drops this $\Delta v$ when converting the dissipation into 'a pointwise lower bound proportional to $\mathcal D(u)$', so the written chain is internally inconsistent. The final display and the stated $\gamma_h$ are nevertheless correct and follow from the sharp versions of both estimates.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the two intermediate estimates by the sharp ones ($\|M\|_{v}^{h,2}\le M_{\max}$ via the normalization, and $\Delta v\,\mathcal D(u)\ge\lambda_N\|u-\bar u\|_{v}^{h,2}$ via the path-graph Poincaré constant), after which the stated $\gamma_h$ follows line by line.
issues.overall_effect: Only the written proof of Proposition 5.1 is unreliable; the stated $\gamma_h$ (used in Assumption 5.2 and Theorem 5.3) is in fact correct, so no downstream result is invalidated.
issues.title: Proof of Proposition 5.1 does not establish the stated coercivity constant (faulty intermediate estimates)
issues.why_classification: The statement and constant are correct and are recovered by one-line sharper local bounds; no lemma, constant, or downstream result changes.

issues.failure_explanation: With $\mathcal T^{(\alpha)}$ and $\mathcal T^{(1/\alpha)}$ defined as centered difference stencils, the operator $\beta\otimes\mathcal T^{(\alpha)}+\beta^{-1}\otimes\mathcal T^{(1/\alpha)}$ has, e.g., coefficient $\beta_p\alpha_{q-1/2}+(\beta_p\alpha_{q-1/2})^{-1}$ on $f_{p,q-1}$, whereas the actual stencil has $(\alpha_{q-1/2}\beta_p)^{-1}$ there; the claimed identity is false for the operator actually used. The correct decomposition of $\mathcal L_h$ uses the one-sided shift operators $(\tilde T w)_q=\Delta v^{-2}(\alpha_{q+1/2}w_{q+1}-\alpha_{q-1/2}w_q)$ and $\Delta v^{-2}(\alpha_{q-1/2}^{-1}w_{q-1}-\alpha_{q+1/2}^{-1}w_q)$, for which the rest of the proof (the spatial-fluctuation estimate and the norm bounds $2\alpha_{\max}/\Delta v^2$, $2/(\alpha_{\min}\Delta v^2)$) goes through unchanged, so the stated $\kappa_h$ bound is true but is not proved by the written decomposition.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redefine the two velocity operators as the one-sided shifts that exactly reproduce the stencil (eq. fp_discrete_separable); the spatial-fluctuation argument and the same operator-norm bounds then yield the stated $\kappa_h$ unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Proposition 5.2, which supplies the fluctuation constant $\kappa_h$ used in Assumption 5.2 and Theorem 5.3, is invalid as written; the stated bound and $\kappa_h$ remain correct via the shift-operator decomposition, so Theorem 5.3's conclusions are not lost.
issues.title: False velocity-operator decomposition in the proof of Proposition 5.2
issues.why_classification: A purely local replacement of the two misidentified operators re-establishes the identical statement and constant; no new argument, lemma, or weakening is needed.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof recalls the L-step update with a minus sign on the advection term, contradicting the actual scheme (eq. L_fd_imex), whose advection term enters with a plus sign (as dictated by the projector-splitting L-subproblem). Consequently the identity (eq. G_derivation), which the theorem invokes as the definition of $G^{n+1}$, is false for the actual scheme: multiplying the true L-step by $X_i^{n+1}$ and summing over $i$ gives $P_X^{n+1}\mathcal L_h^{n+1}(f^{n+1}) = \varepsilon[(f^{n+1}-f^{(2)})/\Delta t - P_X^{n+1}\mathcal A_h(f^{(2)})]$, with the opposite sign on the advection contribution. Since only $\|G^{n+1}\|$ enters the subsequent estimates, the bounds hold with the corrected $G$, but as written the key identity and the theorem's referenced definition of $G^{n+1}$ are wrong.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Flip the sign of the advection term in the recalled L-step and in eq. G_derivation, i.e., define $G^{n+1}=(f^{n+1}-f^{(2)})/\Delta t - P_X^{n+1}\mathcal A_h(f^{(2)})$; all estimates then proceed unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: Only the definition of $G^{n+1}$ in Theorem 5.3 (via eq. G_derivation) is affected; the residual and distance bounds hold verbatim for the correctly-signed residual, and no other result uses this identity.
issues.title: Theorem 5.3's proof mis-signs the L-step advection term, making the definition of $G^{n+1}$ false for the scheme
issues.why_classification: A single forced sign correction, matching the scheme's own L-step, repairs the false identity; the argument is otherwise sign-agnostic (only $\|G\|$ is used), so no conclusion, constant, or guarantee changes.

issues.failure_explanation: Evaluating the prescribed profile on the stated domain $[-1,1]$: at $x=-1$, $\tfrac12(\tanh 15+\tanh(-5))\approx4.5\times10^{-5}$, so $\varepsilon(-1)\approx\varepsilon_0=10^{-3}$; $\varepsilon$ stays within about $1\%$ of $\varepsilon_0$ for $x\lesssim-0.6$, reaches $O(1)$ only on the middle band $x\approx[-0.4,0.3]$, and jumps discontinuously from $\approx0.98$ down to $\varepsilon_0$ at $x=0.3$. The actual profile is thus 'fluid–kinetic–fluid' with an unmentioned discontinuity, not the claimed 'left part of order one, right part small'; the formula does not realize its stated purpose on the left part of the domain.

failure_location.quote: so that the left part of the domain has $\varepsilon(x)$ of order one, while the right part has a smaller, nearly constant value $\varepsilon(x)\approx \varepsilon_0$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the description to match the formula ($\varepsilon=O(1)$ only on a middle band, $\approx\varepsilon_0$ elsewhere, with a jump at $x=0.3$), or replace the formula with one that actually transitions from $O(1)$ on the left to $\varepsilon_0$ on the right of $[-1,1]$.
issues.overall_effect: The description of the mixed-regime test (Section 6.2) misrepresents the profile actually computed. Both $O(1)$- and $\approx\varepsilon_0$-Knudsen regions still occur, so the qualitative low-rank conclusions are not invalidated, but the stated test design is not the one exercised.
issues.title: Mixed-regime Knudsen profile contradicts its stated design
issues.why_classification: Only the test-setup description (or formula) needs a local correction; both regimes remain exercised and no guarantee, rate, or theorem is affected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: a given background charge satisfying the global neutrality condition \(\int_{\Omega_x}(\rho(x,0)-\eta(x))\,\dx=0\)
All numerical tests are performed in a 1D1V phase space with periodic boundary condition in $x$ and zero flux boundary condition in the truncated velocity domain $[-6,6]$.

issues.failure_explanation: The actual initial charge density is $\rho(x,0)=\int f^0\,dv=\rho^0(x)(1+\sqrt{T_{\rm cold}})\approx1.0707\,\rho^0(x)$, because the cold beam Gaussian carries mass $\sqrt{2\pi T_{\rm cold}}$ against $\sqrt{2\pi}$ for the background. Since $\int\rho^0=\int\eta$ by construction (equal constants and equal Gaussian bumps), the neutrality condition fails: $\int(\rho(\cdot,0)-\eta)\,dx=\sqrt{T_{\rm cold}}\int\rho^0\,dx\approx0.0707\,(0.3L+0.1\sqrt\pi)\neq0$ on any domain of length $L$ containing both bumps (about $7\%$ of the total charge). With periodic boundary conditions in $x$, the Poisson equation $-\Delta_x\phi=\rho-\eta$ has no solution at $t=0$, so the described benchmark is ill-posed within the paper's own framework (unlike the other two test setups, whose neutrality is explicitly verified).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Make the data neutral, e.g., rescale $\eta$ so that $\int(\rho(\cdot,0)-\eta)\,dx=0$ with $\rho(x,0)=\rho^0(x)(1+\sqrt{T_{\rm cold}})$, or renormalize $f^0$ so that its velocity integral equals $\rho^0$; the benchmark's character and conclusions are unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The bump-on-tail experiment of Section 6.3 cannot be executed as described (the initial periodic Poisson solve is incompatible); the reported density, field, phase-space, and AP-error results for this benchmark are not reproducible from the stated data without an unstated neutralization step.
issues.title: Bump-on-tail initial data violates the neutrality condition required by the periodic Poisson solve
issues.why_classification: A local rescaling of the test data (or an explicit neutralization step) restores well-posedness without touching the scheme, the analysis, or the qualitative benchmark conclusions.
